original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. A rule's class field accepts one error class or a list of them, and the rule applies to a site of any listed class. The rule match-literal lists missingDecidable and typeMismatch. Decisions B5 and B6 of docs/breaking-changes.md hold.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. LeanMend/Spec/Types.lean Rule has cls : ErrorClass, one class. EVMLean run 21 left ReturnDataBound 3287 as residue with class typeMismatch; the hand bump changed match pc with to match pc.val with there, the edit of match-literal, whose class is missingDecidable.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run lake test: tests/OpsTest.lean shows one rule with two classes proposing candidates at a site of each class, and a rule file with a single class string still loading. A fixture under tests/ with a numeric match that fails as a type mismatch shows match-literal accepted, through a runner that sources tests/lib/report.sh. Run scripts/gate.sh: stdout is one JSON object; the key 'steps.one rule for several error classes.ok' is true, and failed is 0.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Spec and Core import no Shell module (scripts/gate.sh checks it). Termination stays a theorem in LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean, with no retry cap and no timeout as a control. Decision D10 holds: lean-mend adds no declaration to a target. lean-mend depends on Lean core only, not on Mathlib. Every committed text is in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Run export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH" before a lean or lake command. Scratch files go in the gitignored .scratch/ directory, not /tmp. The worker task timeout is 3600 seconds. Do not run lean-mend on EVMLean: one EVMLean run takes about 2 hours, and the operator runs it after the merge.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) LeanMend/Spec/Types.lean, LeanMend/Core/Ops.lean, LeanMend/Shell/Parse.lean, rules/proposed/match-literal.json, docs/rules.md, tests/
restatement: A lean-mend rule can name one error class or a list of error classes in its class field. A rule with a list applies at a site of any listed class, so one rule answers one root cause under every class Lean reports it as. The rule match-literal lists missingDecidable and typeMismatch, so it now proposes its edit for the typeMismatch residue that EVMLean run 21 left behind. A rule file with a single class string still loads. The change must keep the existing limits: Spec and Core import no Shell module, termination stays a theorem with no retry cap or timeout, lean-mend adds no declaration to a target, and lean-mend does not depend on Mathlib. The check scripts/gate.sh must report the step for several error classes as ok with no failed step.
